newsitem.title: UK: Shell jumps to new peak after results.
newsitem.headline: Shell jumps to new peak after results.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc extended initial gains, rising to a record on Thursday after the oil giant posted what were generally seen as a strong set of results for the year, analysts said.
By 1020 GMT, the shares were up 41p to 1102-1/2p, but off their peak of 1110.
Shell reported annual profits as earnings from oil and gas, boosted by higher oil prices and increased production, easily outweighed a substantial fall in profits from chemicals.
Current cost net profit before special items was 5.20 billion pounds ($8.50 billion), while net income on a historical cost basis rose by 30 percent to a record 5.69 billion.

Profits were generally within industry expectations, but the final dividend of 22.5p per share and the improved return on capital were better than expected, said David Stedman, head of research at Daiwa Europe Ltd.
He noted that Shell, whose return on capital has always lagged that of rival British Petroleum Co, rose above 13 percent.
"BP's is still over 15 percent, but Shell is beginning to narrow the gap," Stedman said.
The group also announced share splits and changes in top management at both its Dutch and British units.
"...The net result is a good perception of the figures and I think the Americans will like them too this afternoon," a trader said.
